The test image shows **pod** as the plant part. One pod is split open revealing 2 small pale seeds inside, with a prominent **dark brown/black discoloration at the bottom tip** of the open pod. The pods are dried/mature with typical hairy texture.

Pod-affecting candidates: Anthracnose, Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus, Green_stem_disorder, Phomopsis, Phytophthora, Purple_Seed_Stain, Tobacco_Streak_Virus, White_Mold.

Key feature: dark tip discoloration on pod, seeds look pale/normal (not purple-stained, no white mold).

Top candidates: Anthracnose (dark lesions on pods), Phomopsis (pod infection), Tobacco_Streak_Virus (dark spots on pods).
TSV reference shows dark spots on a green pod — test image has dried/mature pods with dark tip, different pattern. Next: Phomopsis pod.
Phomopsis shows moldy/shriveled seeds inside open pod — test image seeds look intact/pale, no mold. The dark tip in test image is the key feature. Next: Purple_Seed_Stain pod.

Purple Seed Stain reference shows clear purple seed discoloration — test image seeds are pale without purple, so this is not PSS. The dark tip at bottom of pod is the key feature. Final view: Anthracnose leaf reference.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Dried mature soybean pods hanging from stem. One pod split open showing 2 small pale seeds. Prominent **dark brown/black discoloration at bottom tip** of the open pod.

- **TSV pod ref**: Dark spots on green (immature) pods — doesn't match dried/mature pod appearance.
- **Phomopsis pod ref**: Open pod with seed covered in gray-white mold, clearly shriveled — test seeds look intact/pale, no visible mold.
- **Purple Seed Stain pod ref**: Obvious purple discoloration on seeds — test seeds are pale/cream, no purple.
- **Anthracnose leaf ref**: Shows reddish-brown dark lesions on leaf/petiole — the dark concentrated lesion pattern is consistent with Anthracnose, which also causes dark irregular lesions on pods.

**Reasoning**: The key feature is the **localized dark lesion at the pod tip** on a dried, mature pod. White_Mold (no fluffy white growth), PSS (seeds not purple), Phomopsis (seeds not moldy), and TSV (not green pod) are all ruled out. Anthracnose matches best — it causes dark irregular lesions on pods and is a common pod disease in soybean at maturity. The overall presentation (localized dark discoloration on dried pod exterior, seeds pale but small) fits Anthracnose pod infection.
